title: Supplementary Figure 8. Matched support allocation and reference selection.
caption: (a–d) Clinical allocation of each five-donor support set in the paired-cohort benchmark, with the comparator-stratum donor/sample IDs listed for Sepsis, COVID, Giroux and Ji. Excluded Sepsis D2/D4 controls retain their actual identities, PIC01 (pediatric ICU) and IC23 (adult ICU). title: Supplementary Figure 9. Paired-cohort reconstruction and exploratory limits.
caption: (a–g) Composition L1, cell precision, cell coverage, pseudobulk Pearson correlation, classifier two-sample-test AUC (ideal 0.5), MMD² and EN across the four paired cohorts. The adopted 6K/1× model uses five paired support donors, 4,000 cells per test bulk and the original three fixed reference selections. PBISC uses ×1 inputs and support-gated ceiling counts; scSemiProfiler retains its recorded readout. Test/support identities are matched between methods. Individual selections and means±sample standard deviations describe support-selection sensitivity, with three finite values per displayed quality endpoint. (h, i) Observed DEG counts and generated DEG calls in Giroux and Ji explain limits of disease- recovery summaries. Giroux has four unique held-out donors per reference, 10–11 visits and severity/sex confounding; 11 of 12 cell-type/reference comparisons have no observed DEGs. Ji has 13–15 unique donors and 19–26 visits per reference, with 3–228 observed DEGs per comparison. scSemiProfiler has no generated calls in 11 of 12 Ji comparisons, and PBISC in 4 of 12. With no generated calls, precision is undefined; recall and F1 may be zero when observed DEGs exist. Zero detected DEGs do not establish absent biology. Missing values remain undefined; no thresholds are relaxed or values imputed.

title: Supplementary Figure 10. Major-cell immune-program covariance.
caption: (a, b) Sepsis covariance views for PBISC and scSemiProfiler, respectively. (c, d) Corresponding COVID views. Each row contains T-cell, B-cell, monocyte and NK-cell matrices for the same 72 observed-selected immune/state genes per cell type in the original Real-defined order. Upper triangles show Real and lower triangles the generated method; the Real upper triangles are identical between methods. Undefined entries and masked diagonals remain gray; colours span Pearson r from −1 to +1 on the colour scale of Figs 4– 6, and every sixth gene is named. These are means of within-reference correlations, not correlations of averaged expression. Clinical groups are pooled and can drive covariance. title: Supplementary Figure 12. Cell-type-resolved disease effects.
caption: (a–h) Disease contrasts for T cells (a, b), B cells (c, d), monocytes (e, f) and NK cells (g, h) in the paired Sepsis (left) and COVID-19 (right) cohorts, using the first fixed reference selection (D0). Sepsis compares adult/pediatric cases with healthy controls, excluding ICU; COVID-19 compares positive with negative ESKD samples, excluding recovery. The horizontal axis shows fitted TMM/limma-voom log2 fold change, and the vertical axis shows −log10 of each source’s own full-family Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P value. Dashed lines mark adjusted P = 0.05; no fold-change cutoff is applied. Colored points have adjusted P < 0.05 and gray points are not significant. title: Supplementary Figure 13. Cell-type-resolved disease-effect agreement.
caption: (a–h) Mean native disease effects in T cells (a, b), B cells (c, d), monocytes (e, f) and NK cells (g, h) for Sepsis (left) and COVID-19 (right). Each comparison shows PBISC (blue) and scSemiProfiler (green) against the observed reference: the horizontal axis is the observed effect and the vertical axis is the generated effect. Within each reference selection, native effects are defined as log2(1 + mean donor-condition CP10K in cases) minus log2(1 + mean donor-condition CP10K in controls). Effects are then averaged equally across the three fixed selections: Sepsis D0/D1/D3 and COVID-19 D0/D1/D4. Each cohort and cell type uses the intersection of observed testing-family genes across its three selections, without filtering by generated testability or DEG significance. Hexagonal bins summarize gene density in the central window (−1 to +1 on both axes); insets show the full effect range. Pearson correlation, Lin concordance correlation (CCC) and the reported gene counts use the entire observed-defined gene set, including genes outside the central window. Native zero effects are retained. These descriptive mean effects differ from the fitted voom coefficients in the volcano plots; no P values or adjusted P values are averaged. Existing effects, agreement summaries and density-bin counts are reused without refitting. Reference-selection variation is not independent biological replication.

title: Supplementary Figure 22. Peak severity and mortality associations using patient-
caption: mean fractions in four public COVID-19 cohorts This peak-severity and patient-mean analysis uses four public adult COVID-19 PBMC single-cell cohorts: Stephenson 2021 (Newcastle, Cambridge and London; n = 73, 6 deaths; donor CV0198, who has a malignant B-cell population, is excluded, as C116 and C139 are in Fig. 7), COMBAT 2022 (Oxford and London; n = 75, 7 deaths), van der Wijst 2021 (San Francisco; n = 42, 7 deaths) and Liu 2021 (Bethesda; n = 29, 3 deaths); 219 patients with a severity grade and 23 deaths in total. Cell labels are each study's own annotation in its public CELLxGENE file. For each patient, the percentage of PBMCs in each population (red cells, platelets and malignant B cells removed) is averaged over acute-phase samples with at least 500 cells (Stephenson 2021, collected before day 28 of the study; COMBAT 2022 and Liu 2021, within 28 days of symptom onset or with no onset date; van der Wijst 2021, with reported days_from_start ≤14, counting missing values as zero). Peak severity is placed on a common scale with death = 10: Stephenson 2021 worst clinical status (asymptomatic 1, mild 4, moderate 5, severe 6, critical 7), COMBAT 2022 outcome (not hospitalized 2, hospitalized without oxygen 4, with oxygen 5, non-invasive ventilation 6, intubated 7), van der Wijst 2021 highest NIH ordinal score (4–7) and Liu 2021 severity (moderate 4.5, severe 5.5, critical 7). Severity is tested by Spearman ρ and death by the Mann–Whitney AUC. Death is a recorded death (COMBAT 2022, also death within 28 days) and is analysed in the patients with a severity grade: the 11 London patients of Stephenson 2021, who have neither a grade nor a recorded outcome, are left out, and the 11 other Stephenson 2021 patients whose final outcome is unknown (worst status not death) count as survivors. Cohorts are pooled by DerSimonian–Laird random-effects meta-analysis of Fisher z (standard error √(1.06/(n − 3))) and of AUC − 0.5 (Hanley–McNeil standard error, at least 0.035); k is the number of cohorts and N the number of patients pooled. ESKD: the source-priority patient-mean cohort of Fig. 7 (n = 66; 11 deaths; normal scores within source) with the same population definitions. Filled markers, P < 0.05; open markers, P ≥ 0.05; lines, 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap with 2,000 resamples for ESKD and 1,500 for single cohorts; random-effects intervals for meta-analyses). (a) Spearman ρ with peak severity in ESKD (squares), in each public cohort (grey circles) and in the meta-analysis (diamonds; values on the right) for the anchors, the prespecified populations evaluated externally (including NK CD56dim and CD16 mono C1). B ASC total stands for B ASC IgG and IgA, which only Stephenson 2021 resolves (b); CD16 mono is the percentage of monocytes. (b) B ASC subsets in Stephenson 2021: Spearman ρ with peak severity in ESKD and in Stephenson 2021 (left), and the odds ratio per severity step (1–3, 4–5, 6–9, death) from a quasi- binomial model of cell counts adjusted for age, sex and site (right). (c) Meta-analysed AUC for death in all patients (diamonds) and in patients with peak severity ≥ 6 (triangles, dashed lines). (d) HSPC AUC for death from each patient's first acute sample (grey) or the mean of samples taken more than 7 days after onset (black), with deaths/patients; Liu 2021 does not resolve HSPC. * Public labels used: B ASC dividing, Plasmablast (Stephenson 2021) and PB_Prolif (van der Wijst 2021); T CD8 CM, CD8.EM (Stephenson 2021, which has no CD8 central-memory cluster) and CD8.TCM with CD8.TCM.CCL5 (COMBAT 2022); T CD8 CTL, CD8.TE (Stephenson 2021), CD8.TEMRA, CD8.TEFF and CD8.TEM (COMBAT 2022), T8_Mem (van der Wijst 2021) and CD8 memory T cells (Liu 2021). All P values are two-sided and not corrected for multiple testing. Supplementary Fig. 27 gives the multiplicity-adjusted external comparisons for draw-day grade and last-draw mortality.
